1.explanation:
The inconsistent handling of comments on `case` vs. `default` labels arises in the printer logic for switch statements, which lives in `src/language-js/print/statement.js`.  

That file contains the code that renders each `SwitchCase` node (including the `default:` branch). It decides when to break the line and when to attach comments inline. Because the logic for `default` is (unintentionally) slightly different than for `case`—forcing a line break before the comment—it needs to be adjusted there so that `default:` comments are treated the same way as `case:` comments.

2.explanation: The formatting logic for switch cases—including the special `default` node—lives in src/language-js/print/statement.js where the printer builds the `case`/`default` header and attaches comments. That file currently treats the `default` clause’s trailing comment differently, forcing it onto the next line. The comment-handling utilities in src/language-js/print/comment.js control how comments are bound as trailing or dangling; they play a role in determining whether a `//` comment stays on the same line after a colon. Fixing this bug requires adjusting the SwitchCase printing in statement.js so that it uses the same inline-trailing-comment logic as for `case`, and if necessary tweaking the comment-placement rules in comment.js to ensure the `default: // ...` stays together.
2.bug_scenario:
When formatting a JavaScript switch statement, Prettier preserves inline comments after the colon on `case` clauses (e.g. `case X: // comment`) but for the `default` clause it pulls the comment onto its own line. In other words, given

  switch (x) {
    case A: // ok inline comment
      …
    default: // should stay inline
      …
  }

Prettier currently rewrites the `default` so the `// comment` lives on the next line. The expected behavior is to keep the default’s trailing comment on the same line, exactly as it does for ordinary `case` clauses.
